top_story: Israel’s push for mass Palestinian expulsion from Gaza sharpened over the past two days, moving from the defence minister’s effort to secure Donald Trump’s backing on 2 September to Itamar Ben-Gvir’s public endorsement on 3 September, signaling that forced transfer is shifting from fringe rhetoric toward an articulated policy drive. That trajectory deepens Palestinian fears of permanent dispossession and raises pressure on Arab governments already balancing public anger with strategic ties to Israel and Washington. In parallel, the deadly missile strike on a wedding in southern Iran has intensified confrontation with the United States, feeding a regional climate in which civilian harm is becoming politically instrumentalized as well as militarily consequential. The UN finding on 4 September that UAE-linked networks supplied weapons and foreign fighters to Sudan’s RSF underscores a wider pattern: regional powers are not containing conflict but extending it across borders, with civilians bearing the cost from Gaza and Iran to Sudan.
